candidates.summary: a frame refused inside a card, or a second refused card opener in one column, still lets a `</gno-frame>` end the outer frame and push its grid out, the shape the refused-card fix was for
candidates.failure_scenario: Input `<gno-frame>` `<gno-columns>` `<gno-frame>` `<gno-frame>` `x` `</gno-frame>` `</gno-frame>` `<gno-columns-sep>` `b` `</gno-columns>` `</gno-frame>` `after`, one per line. The card opens (case at 243); the nested opener is refused but the refused case at 254 requires `!frameInner(pc)`, so nothing is remembered; the nested close closes the card (246); the card's own close then hits `kind == frameTagClose && open` (251) and calls endFrame while the frame's grid is open. wrapFrames then breaks at the grid (gridCloseInFrame meets the outer close first), so the page renders an empty `<section class="gno-frame"></section>`, the grid outside it, an invalid comment in column 0 and a trailing invalid comment: the output invalid_card_at_depth_cap had before this round. Golden invalid_frame_in_card only avoids it by giving the card no close of its own. Same result with `<gno-frame x="1">` then `<gno-frame x="2">` in one column, each closed: frameRefusedKey is a bool, so the second close ends the outer frame. An author who nests a box in a card, which the docs refuse, loses the outer frame's border around the whole grid.
candidates.verify_by: Add golden/ext_frame/invalid_frame_in_card_closed.md.txtar with the input above and an empty output.html, run `go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown/ -run TestGnoExtension -update-golden-tests -count=1` in a scratch tree, read the written output: expect the grid inside the section as in invalid_card_attrs_keeps_frame, observe `<section class="gno-frame">\n</section>\n<div class="gno-columns">` and a trailing `<!-- unexpected/invalid frame tag omitted -->`; repeat with the two-attribute-opener input. Fix: remember a frame refused inside the card in its own flag, tested ahead of the inner-close case at 246, and count refusals instead of a bool.
